subject: NAACP Presidential Interview and Spoken Word Showcase
overview: The West Medford Community Center hosted a First Fridays program featuring an interview with the new Mystic Valley NAACP President Jillian Harvey. The event also included a spoken word performance by three female artists to celebrate Women’s History Month.

items.title: Community Engagement and Historical Trauma
items.summary: Frances Nwajei discussed the importance of proactive community engagement by city officials to build relationships and address historical trauma.

items.title: Interview with Jillian Harvey
items.summary: Jillian Harvey described her path into municipal leadership and her work establishing a Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion division in the town of Arlington.

items.title: Mystic Valley NAACP Leadership
items.summary: Harvey shared her vision for the Mystic Valley NAACP, focusing on increasing membership, revitalizing the youth council, and prioritizing voter registration.

items.title: Women’s History Month Spoken Word Performance
items.summary: Spoken word artists Michelle La Poetica, Cole Rodriguez, and Dexter Garcia performed original poetry regarding identity, social justice, and environmental conservation.

items.title: WMCC Community Announcements
items.summary: Terry Carter provided updates on upcoming community center events, including a scholarship tea, a legislative breakfast forum, and a West Medford family reunion.
